answer.rationale: Finance mandate requires an 18% cost cut, so I cannot lock in an incumbent that has historically held cost flat (c1) or only realized savings through negotiation (c4). Memory c2 documents a prior successful switch to a low-cost vendor where onboarding was quick and invoicing stayed accurate — directly relevant to a primary-source transition. Memory c6 shows that multi-year incumbent commitments cut unit cost, but extending that pattern would not deliver an 18% reduction and would not be available within 14 days anyway. The contract expires without auto-renew, so I must actively select a vendor rather than rely on renewal. The assembly line at 94% with no buffer raises delivery risk, which argues against a disruptive switch. I will verify c2 and c6 to confirm that the c2 switch was on a comparable component/cycle and that c6's pricing gains would not close the gap. If the archive confirms c2's switch was clean and on-time, and c6 pricing gains are insufficient against the 18% target, I will proceed with switch_primary_vendor to a qualified low-cost supplier, with a tight transition window and explicit delivery-SLA terms to protect the 94% throughput.
